(a) Section 3(n) of such Act is amended by striking out “, except as used in subsection (s) (1),”. 
    (b) Section 13(a) of such Act is amended—

        (1) 
by redesignating paragraphs (11), (13), (14), (15), and (21) as paragraphs (10), (11), (12), (13), and (14), respectively, and
 
        (2) 
by striking out or” at the end of paragraph (14) (as so redesignated in this subsection) and inserting in lieu thereof a period.  
    (c) Paragraph (7) of section 13(a) of such Act is amended by striking out “or order” and inserting in lieu thereof “, order, or certificate”.

fable.w: The section makes only technical and conforming amendments: it strikes a phrase, redesignates paragraphs, and changes "or order" to ", order, or certificate". The mention of an order or certificate might suggest an administrative process, but the text sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the structure and wording of other sections of an Act, such as redesignating paragraphs and inserting punctuation. It does not establish any mechanism for public comment, consultation, hearings, or advisory committees involving non-federal parties. Therefore, it does not involve participation.

(b) Section 13(a) of such Act is amended— (1) by redesignating paragraphs (11), (13), (14), (15), and (21) as paragraphs (10), (11), (12), (13), and (14), respectively, and (2) by striking out or” at the end of paragraph (14) (as so redesignated in this subsection) and inserting in lieu thereof a period. (c) Paragraph (7) of section 13(a) of such Act is amended by striking out “or order” and inserting in lieu thereof “, order, or certificate”.
qwen_block.b:
Temptation: The text contains the word "order" and "certificate," which might suggest some form of administrative proceeding or public interaction. However, these are merely terms being inserted into a list of definitions or regulatory instruments within the statute itself.

Resolution: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the structure and wording of other sections of an Act (redesignating paragraphs, striking out words, inserting punctuation). It does not create any new process for public comment, consultation, hearings, or advisory committees. It is purely legislative housekeeping.

opus.w: The section only makes technical edits: it strikes cross-reference language, renumbers paragraphs and adds "certificate" to an existing list. Nothing in it brings anyone outside the federal government into a federal decision. The change to paragraph (7) might look like rulemaking authority, but it grants no new power to issue regulations and requires no hearing, comment or consultation.
opus.s: Paragraph (7) of section 13(a) of such Act is amended by striking out “or order” and inserting in lieu thereof “, order, or certificate”.

It gives no new authority to issue regulations and creates no comment period, hearing, consultation or right to sue. The rest of the section just strikes words and renumbers paragraphs.
